Search found related evidence, but no direct demonstration of the exact constrained setup: a GRU next-item recommender with title/description encoders trained from scratch. [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116) jointly trains a GRU text encoder with collaborative recommendation, supporting task-specific text representations; however, its GRU encodes document words rather than interaction histories, and experiments initialize word embeddings with CBOW trained on an external abstract corpus. [ITS-Rec](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) reports descriptions contributing more than titles, but uses frozen pretrained BERT, a Transformer backbone, and reviews. Its gains therefore do not establish benefits under this benchmark’s restrictions.

A reasonable experimental hypothesis is a small, randomly initialized token embedding layer plus masked mean pooling or a shallow CNN over titles/descriptions, projected into item-ID representations and jointly optimized inside one GRU4Rec network using next-item loss. Preserve model-number and connector tokens that might distinguish Electronics products; compare against the ID-only baseline using the fixed macro validation HR@10. These are proposed adaptations, not verified improvements. [Personalized Complementary Product Recommendation](https://www.amazon.science/publications/personalized-complementary-product-recommendation) supports learning product relationships alongside personal purchase history, but uses a different architecture and supervision. Text similarity alone does not establish complementarity, physical compatibility, ownership, or satisfaction; any benefit must come from improved prediction of observed interactions.
